customer_question: Our new design variant changes the PCB board size, adds components, changes enclosure dimensions, and/or changes artwork (buzzer peripheral circuit, programming connector) - but the FW on the MCU and BLE chip is unchanged and the BLE-to-antenna wiring and components are unchanged. Can this be added to the existing Product List for free as a derivative model?
question_variants: Do PCB board size changes require a new Bluetooth test or registration?
Can we add a new variant with the same BLE FW and antenna path as the base model to the Product List for free?
Does changing the enclosure/casing size alongside a board size change affect Bluetooth certification status?
We changed buzzer circuitry and the programming connector but not the BLE path - is this a free derivative?
actual_issue: Multiple design change scenarios were asked about across this thread (sensor 4 concept, enclosure size changes, artwork changes), all sharing a common question: given specific design changes that don't touch the BLE FW or BLE-to-antenna path, can the new variant be added to the existing Product List as a free derivative? The consultant consistently applied the same rule: if the FW on the MCU (IC100) and BLE chip (IC10) is the same as the base registration AND there are no changes to components or routing between the BLE chip and the antenna, then the new variant qualifies for free Product List addition regardless of other changes (board size, enclosure size, 5V boost circuit addition, buzzer circuit change, programming connector change, PCB coaxial connector for radio certification testing). Each time, the consultant confirmed no additional testing is required and only the free web-based Product List addition operation is needed to complete Bluetooth certification for the new variant.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth certification is concerned with changes that affect the Bluetooth radio's actual RF behavior (as defined by the Bluetooth specification: protocol/profile stack, and RF PHY performance). Changes outside this scope - even significant mechanical or circuit changes - don't require new testing or registration, as long as: (1) the firmware running on the MCU and BLE chip is identical to the already-registered base design, and (2) the circuit between the BLE chip and the antenna (routing, components such as matching network) is unchanged. Changes that are clearly outside this scope and thus don't require re-testing include: PCB board size changes, additions of non-BLE components (e.g., 5V boost circuits, stroke sensors), changes to the product enclosure/casing dimensions, changes to PCB artwork in non-BLE areas (buzzer circuits, programming/firmware-write connectors), and changes to the PCB coaxial connector used only for Japanese radio certification testing. In all these cases, the new variant can be added to the existing registration's Product List for free via a simple web operation.
consultant_answer: For Bluetooth certification registration, if the FW on IC100 and IC10 is the same as the base registration, then regardless of additional tests, the new product can be added to the Product List for free as a derivative. If the BLE circuit routing and components are also unchanged, only the free Product List addition operation is needed to complete Bluetooth certification for the new variant. / For Bluetooth logo certification, if there are no changes to the protocol/profile components defined in the Bluetooth specification, the variant can be added to the existing registration's Product List for free. All the changes in the attached file are outside Bluetooth specification scope - free Product List addition is fine. No procedures beyond Product List addition are needed for these changes. / If 'the FW on the MCU and BLE chip is the same as the base registration AND there are no changes to BLE-antenna path components or routing,' free derivative registration is possible.
decision_logic: Apply a two-condition test to determine if a design change qualifies as a free derivative: (1) Is the FW on the MCU and BLE chip identical to the base registration? (2) Are the components and routing between the BLE chip and the antenna unchanged? If both are yes, the change is outside Bluetooth specification scope regardless of what else changed (board size, enclosure, non-BLE circuitry, PCB artwork in non-BLE areas) and the new variant can be added to the existing Product List for free with no additional testing.
final_recommendation: If a customer's design change satisfies both conditions (same BLE FW and unchanged BLE-to-antenna path), confirm they qualify for free Product List addition as a derivative model with no additional testing, and direct them to the Qualification Workspace derivative addition procedure document. Explicitly state that changes to board size, enclosure size, non-BLE components, and non-BLE circuit areas (buzzer circuits, programming connectors, test coaxial connectors) do not affect this eligibility.
risk_if_done_wrong: If a customer unnecessarily performs a new registration or testing for a design change that qualifies as a free derivative, they incur avoidable cost and delay. Conversely, if a change that does affect the BLE-antenna path or FW is incorrectly classified as a free derivative, the product could be sold with an invalid Bluetooth certification.
